dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1799 that reach 3 or more papers, and those of 1798 over the 1799 pages, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 520 items, 515 printed somewhere, 137 reaching 4 papers by the finder's counts; items_from_1798.json: 387 items, 80 printed somewhere). Every finder item in 3 or more papers was counted again by the first 40 words of its opening against every page of 1799 in both transcriptions (a page prints the item when it holds at least 18 of the opening's word 5-grams), and texts read from different printings were merged (393 texts, 114 at the bar by that count). For the texts one paper short of the bar (228) and those at the bar without every surviving paper (101), the missing papers were looked for again on their pages, by the text's words (the best page within its weeks) and by its names, and the strong candidates read. A sweep of seven-word sequences shared by 4 or more papers, over every page, found 1,483 clusters; the 82 passages that no finder item explains were read. The runs of foreign news that every surviving paper printed in July and August were counted paragraph by paragraph, each by its own opening (textcount.py), and the items at the bar were counted again by their openings read on their pages; printings on pages whose transcriptions are garbled or filed under another page were read by eye.
dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (Y-THIN), as amended by the owner on 23 November 2026 (choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks (those with a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and by at least 4; items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted; the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news; digests are not admitted. Single paragraphs from runs of news are counted by their own words (C-09). In 1799 only four papers survive from July to the end of August, and they reprinted whole runs of foreign news, so 36 items are admitted by the rule's first part, most of them in July and August; 8 eligible items are chosen for the months and the kinds of news the admitted items do not reach (January to April, June, November, and the President's speech in December).
dispositions.paper_counting: 1799 has 10 catalogue series, which are 9 papers: the Gazette of the United States, & Philadelphia Daily Advertiser (Philadelphia; a daily, 264 issues, to 20 December), the Providence Journal (52), the New Hampshire Gazette (Portsmouth; 52), the Portland Gazette under two numbers ('The Gazette', 16 issues to 22 April, and 'Jenks's Portland Gazette', 36 from 29 April: one paper), the Kentucky Gazette (Lexington; 19, to 9 May), the Mirror (Concord, N.H.; 11), the Republican Ledger (Portsmouth, N.H.; 11, from 19 September), the Virginia Argus (Richmond; 9) and the Eagle (Hanover, N.H.; 2). Papers in print in any three weeks: 5 to 8 from January to June; 4 from 9 July to 29 August (the Gazette of the United States, the New Hampshire Gazette, the Portland Gazette and the Providence Journal); 4 to 6 from September; fewer after 20 December, when the Gazette of the United States has no surviving issue. The bar is 4 papers in every week (5 for items first printed on 1 January).

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: The 44 admitted and chosen items, the 89 eligible items not chosen, the 2 for the owner and the 25 read below the bar were counted by the first 40 words of their own openings against every page in both transcriptions, and the papers the comparison missed were looked for again and read; their papers are in counted_items.json.
counted_item_by_item.Paragraphs in runs of news: Foreign news reached the papers in runs of short paragraphs under London, Paris, Vienna, Hamburg and Italian datelines, which the Gazette of the United States, the New Hampshire Gazette, the Portland Gazette and the Providence Journal reprinted whole, in much the same order, in late July and August (C-09). Each paragraph is counted by its own opening: 32 of the 36 admitted items are single paragraphs or letters from such runs.
counted_item_by_item.One report in two wordings, or abridged: Captain Freeman's news of the fleets (Boston, July: two wordings), the paragraph on the President's visit to Fort Independent (the Providence Journal in its own words), the report of the President's nomination of a minister to France (two wordings) and the Havana circular (under two introductions) are each counted as one item (C-02); the Portland Gazette prints the Trent paragraph of 7 May and the Roveredo paragraph without their first sentences, counted with them, as 1773 counted the Massachusetts Spy's paragraph on the Sheriffs' letter.
counted_item_by_item.Pages that are not printings: Pages that only quote an item are not counted (C-07): the Governor of Pennsylvania's message of March quoting the President's proclamation of 12 March; the address of the minority of the Virginia legislature, which quotes the Sedition Act and a Virginia law of 1785 (counted as one text, by its own opening); later paragraphs that quote the reports of the Secretaries.
counted_item_by_item.Repeated printings and misfiled transcri: The Gazette of the United States prints the President's proclamation of 12 March in two issues; both printings are in the ledger. The Portland Gazette of 26 August has the RevX transcriptions of its pages 2 and 3 filed one page on (in the release's revx_page_map), so its ten printings on page 2 are cut from the CA text, as is the Providence Journal's page 3 of 27 February, whose RevX text lacks the item.
counted_item_by_item.A digest: 'Hamburg Summaries' (Lower Elbe, 22 June), printed by all four papers of its weeks, is a summary of the Vienna Court Gazettes and other news: a digest, not admitted (C-09).
